reason: I'd probably start the free 14 days since there's no auto-charge, but I've tried enough sleep apps that I don't expect it to beat the free sounds I already use, and with my bedtime moving every week I doubt it learns my timing in two weeks. On my income I'd most likely just stay on the free version.
objection: The 'minutes you fell asleep faster' number comes from my own groggy morning check, so it feels like the app grading itself. Is that real improvement or just marketing?
would_change_my_mind: If my own 14-day record clearly showed I was falling asleep 10+ minutes faster, even on the weeks my schedule shifted, I'd pay the 4,900 won.
